Because EM has a replacement of spaces in "Name" value (https://github.com/openbmc/entity-manager/blob/2826f40187e4090acd761b59bc4c6f0036b7be8c/src/overlay.cpp#L241), mux name in the symlink can be different from the config. My preference is that we don't add yet more free functions to Utils.h. It's not a maintainable path forward.

Rather, keeping things that are together together via a coherent object model makes this all much more comprehensible, and allows us to encode relationships between concepts in the type system. I'd much prefer we create a `I2CMux` object that has a `const` `bus()` method that returns an `I2CBus` object, from which you can retrieve the bus index (... because it's a property of a Linux I2C bus ...).

`uint64_t` was used since entity-manager and most of the sensors in dbus-sensors uses `uint64_t` when it comes to describing the bus. However, looking into the kernel, it looks like `int` is used:
https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/6c52d4da1c742cd01a797a4d0a2d3c5a60dc9bfe/drivers/i2c/i2c-core-base.c#L1644

`int` could be used instead, but perhaps a separate CL to change all the variables that describe bus in dbus-sensors and entity-manager to `int`.

What if I moved it into DeviceMgmt.cpp as it seems more fitting to have a function that retrieves the bus in that file. I don't think we need to create an `I2CMux` and `I2CBus` object for a function, but perhaps I don't see what you are trying to illustrate.

Part of where I was going with the other comment about an `I2CBus` object was that with that the representation would be encapsulated (and we can collect operations related to I2C buses on the class).

In the past I've written this, which probably provides some context for my position:

https://github.com/ibm-openbmc/platform-fru-detect/blob/main/src/sysfs/i2c.hpp

If an `I2CBus` object will be made that will be used by the sensors that use bus, should we standardize all those that use bus to use a specific data type? Currently different data types are used by different sensors.

unsigned int: Fan
uint64_t: HwMon, IntelCPU, and PSU
int: Intrusion, NVMe
uint8_t MCUTemp

Since the kernel uses int would it be fine to use int for `I2CBus`?

Just to clarify, I'm not expecting that you do the rework to integrate the type throughout the code base. But if we at least bring it into existence and start using it in code you're changing, then we can spread its use over time.

I think we should settle on `int` for the bus index type, as this is what the kernel uses.

The idea behind `std::optional` was so that we could return an empty optional instance instead of throwing an exception. A couple of suggestions for alternatives:

1. Log an error, and then `return {};`
2. Given libc now provides `std::expected` (relatively recent, over the course of us reviewing this patch), use `std::expected` instead of `std::optional`: https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/utility/expected

This applies to the exception cases below.
I log an error and `return std::nullopt;` since we are returning a `std::optional`
Done
Wait, we should never be causing exceptions that we then catch ourselves. Please instead perform an early return for the error cases.

Hi @jonico.eustaquio@fii-na.com, I updated https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/69030/7 to adapt new changes to the schemas from Hansen. I will need to update more as more changes are on their way. Just in case you might want to take a look.

There is a concern about limiting the support for ```MuxChannel``` and the i2c devices behind it to only dbus-sensors.

https://discord.com/channels/775381525260664832/1187158775438778408/1377610867423842415

There are other devices which may be handled by other daemons such as Voltage regulators (implemented in phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt) which will not be able to use the code here for ```MuxChannel``` support.

Essentially most daemons consuming ```Bus``` property today would need to be capable to consume ```MuxChannel``` property.

I see at least 2 options if people want to create a more general solution which can work for all daemons.

1) Handle the mux internally in EM and expose ```Bus``` field as before which is just the ```MuxChannel``` property resolved by EM at runtime. That will not require any changes to existing daemons to be able to access devices behind the mux.

2) Write some configuration parsing library which can then be pulled in by daemons to resolve their ```MuxChannel``` properties into a concrete ```Bus```.
